School & learning

irregular adjective

also irregular verb, irregularly

classical

Traupman 334

inaequālis, inaequāle

irregular, uneven, unequal

Classically “uneven, unequal”; Traupman uses it of irregular verbs and declensions. Irregularly, inaequāliter.

Examples

  • inaequāle verbum (ut “volō”)

    an irregular verb (like volō, I want)Traupman 334

  • “Duo” inaequāliter dēclīnātur.

    “Duo” is irregularly declined.Traupman 334

See also grammar, declension.

SourcesLewis & Short: inaequalis

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 334.
